html:
The Indian National Congress is a political party founded in Bombay in December 1885 as a meeting of educated Indians. It became the main force of the independence movement and ruled India for most of the decades after 1947.

At its first session 72 delegates met, encouraged by a retired British official, Allan Octavian Hume. Early leaders such as Dadabhai Naoroji asked politely for reforms and argued that British rule drained India's wealth. Radicals such as Bal Gangadhar Tilak wanted more, and the party split for a time in 1907.

After 1920 Gandhi turned it into a mass movement of peasants and townspeople. Its great campaigns were:

  • Non cooperation, 1920 to 1922.
  • The Salt March and civil disobedience, from 1930.
  • Quit India, 1942.

It held that it spoke for all Indians, a claim the Muslim League rejected, and that clash ended in the Partition of India. After independence it governed under Nehru, then his daughter Indira Gandhi and her heirs, almost without a break until 1977, and often after.
sum: The Indian National Congress is a political party founded in Bombay in December 1885 as a meeting of educated Indians. It became the main force of the independence movement and ruled India for most of the decades after 1947.
